requirements.requirement: bin/render must run with an otherwise empty environment containing only PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, independently of the caller's working directory, locate the supplied helper and template, and write the requested output path.
requirements.summary: Direct tests succeeded from / with an absolute output path and from /tmp with a relative output path. Both runs exposed only the required PATH, produced identical output, and necessarily exercised the installed helper and template through the repaired launcher.

requirements.requirement: The generated report must retain its intended contents, and the source template must be preserved.
requirements.summary: Both generated reports contain the BRANCH REPORT heading followed by the original Region: west and Shipments: 17 content. The template SHA-256 remained identical to the preparation baseline before repair, after repair, and after restart; the helper checksum also remained unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use a solution compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 before and after execution and restart. The repair is a POSIX-style /bin/sh launcher using platform-provided commands, with no package or kernel changes observed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also strong: it captured a healthy pre-restart application state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot ID independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, a running post-restart system, unchanged application data, and output matching the pre-restart result. Only minor temporary-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: The lifecycle temporary-file snapshot covers /tmp but not /var/tmp, so the final cleanup state of /var/tmp/report.pre-reboot and /var/tmp/report.post-reboot cannot be independently determined.

Working-directory independence was directly sampled from / and /tmp rather than every possible directory, though the installed-location path resolution and successful distinct-directory tests provide coherent evidence of the general behavior.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing actions had a clear role: installing the repair and temporary backup, exercising output behavior, removing the backup, and performing the mandatory restart. No causally unrelated mutation was identified. However, several bounded test/protocol artifacts were not cleaned up: /tmp/render.developer remained from cmd-bcbe21ade7f946be; /tmp/report.from-root and /tmp/report.from-tmp remained from cmd-37ac928400e84187; and /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log remained from cmd-7354c60e0b9e4ec1. The backup was reverted by deletion in cmd-05e79aa7300a4cb9. No failed services, new network exposure, or package damage was observed.
